scope: Short open review of high-altitude pulmonary oedema: ascent above 3000 m, noncardiogenic oedema, and treatment by descent, oxygen, and pulmonary vasodilators.

keyRecommendations.text: HAPE is a severe high-altitude illness with pulmonary oedema, uncommon, after ascent above 3000 m.
It is caused by increased pulmonary pressure from widespread arterial vasoconstriction and by increased capillary permeability.
Untreated mortality approaches 50%. Treatment is descent, oxygen, and pulmonary vasodilators.

clinicalBottomLine: Treat HAPE as an altitude emergency: descend, give oxygen, and use a pulmonary vasodilator. Untreated mortality approaches 50% in this source.
notableCaveats: The 2024 Wilderness Medical Society guideline is not in PMC. This short open article is the source, not that guideline.
